reason: The text demonstrates a well-defined and valued hierarchical structure. Moses exercises clear command authority over Joshua (וַיֹּאמֶר מֹשֶׁה אֶל־יְהוֹשֻׁעַ 'Moses said to Joshua'), who obeys without question (וַיַּעַשׂ יְהוֹשֻׁעַ כַּאֲשֶׁר אָמַר־לוֹ מֹשֶׁה 'Joshua did as Moses had said'). The passage also assigns specific roles within a hierarchy: Joshua as military commander, Moses as the spiritual leader holding God's rod, and Aaron and Hur in explicitly supportive positions (תָּמְכוּ בְיָדָיו 'sustained his hands'). The text implies that Israel's victory is directly contingent upon maintaining this hierarchical structure and each person's faithful adherence to their designated role. Nothing suggests hierarchy is unimportant or discouraged.
